Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: DPA + hosting geography questions for pilot

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the pilot was helpful. Before procurement can move forward we have a handful of privacy/security gating items the legal team flagged around transfers and hosting:

1) Can Redwood commit to keeping EU customer data in the EU for the pilot? If not, we need a clear Data Export Annex that lays out the fallback routing to non-EU regions and the business justification process for any export.
2) We need a current subprocessor list and SOC 2 evidence (or equivalent).
3) For key management: can customers require an EU-only KMS or customer-managed keys for the pilot instance?
4) SCCs: we need to see specific SCC language you propose (Article 46 alternatives were discussed internally) and any UK Addendum if applicable.

We attach our questionnaire (Novocare_DPA_Questions.pdf). Procurement would like to understand whether the MSA/order form redlines will be manageable within a two-week window.

Can you loop in legal and sales and share a proposed redline and recommended path forward (hosted + contractual safeguards vs private deploy)?

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Procurement (Novocare Health)

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (sales) for procurement/timing and Laura (legal) for redlines. Wanted to propose an approach so procurement can pick a path quickly: 

Option A — Hosted with contractual guarantees (recommended for speed):
- Redwood commits to EU-region processing for the pilot (data residency) in the Order Form and adds a Data Export Annex that requires explicit, documented approval for any routing outside EU.
- Execute the standard EU SCCs (2021 clauses) + an explicit Transfer Impact Addendum limited to the pilot scope.
- Provide current subprocessor list and SOC 2 Type II report; provide KMS options (customer-managed keys via bring-your-own-key is available, but specific EU-only key separation will require a tech configuration addendum and a small setup lead time).

Option B — Private deployment (longer lead time, higher cost):
- Dedicated private deployment in client's VPC or Redwood Private in an EU zone and customer-managed KMS. This eliminates the need for SCCs for transfers, but procurement must accept a dedicated-reservation contract and a multi-week provisioning window.

Immediate asks from our side to move forward: 
- Marta/procurement: confirm preferred option (A or B) and target procurement cutoff date.
- We will deliver an initial redline for the DPA (attached) that reflects Option A language and a short Data Export Annex. Laura, please pick up legal redline and review for UK Addendum implications.

I attach our proposed edits for your review (redwood_proposed_dpa_redline.docx). If you confirm Option A, we can aim for a two-week legal/procurement cycle; Option B will need ~4–6 weeks.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with Laura and Ben internally right after this.

— Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Internal quick note — few commercial points to flag for Irene/Laura: 

- If Novocare requires EU-only KMS separation (BYOK with an EU HSM), we should budget an onboarding surcharge (one-time setup + monthly key-tenant cost). Estimate: setup USD 6k–10k, monthly USD 1k–2k depending on HSM vendor.
- Option A (hosted + annex) keeps the deal in the standard hosted pricing band and should be the fastest to close. We can accept the Data Export Annex language but want the annex to include a clear escalation path (product + CS approval) and a maximum approval SLA for export requests (48–72 hours).
- Procurement timeline: if Novocare can sign LOI/PO by 20 Jun we can hit a 1 July pilot start. If they push to Option B, that moves the start to mid-August.

Laura — can you confirm the redline turn for legal? Irene suggested two weeks for Option A. If we can get a legal redline by Friday (13 Jun), I will push procurement to match the 20 Jun PO target.

Thanks — Ben.
